note: Three warships whose sea-trial power and speed are transcribed from a published record. The set stays tiny on purpose: it pins the model's error against measured trials, it is not a fitting set.

cases.name: HMS Dreadnought (1906)
cases.source: Royal Navy trials, 9 October 1906, as transcribed by Wikipedia (HMS Dreadnought (1906))
cases.note: The 146-case reference set lists this hull at Cb 0.61; a form-derived Cb near 0.54 would give +7.7 % instead, so the block coefficient is itself a source of a couple of points.

cases.name: HMS Hood (1920)
cases.source: 1920 full power trial at 42,200 t: 151,280 shp for 32.07 kn (three-hour full power trial averaged 150,473 shp at 31.79 kn); transcribed from the Hood Association / trial summary records
cases.note: The full power trial gives 151,280 shp at 32.07 kn on 42,200 t; a three-hour full power trial averaged 150,473 shp at 31.79 kn. The earlier record used 'over 150,000 shp', a lower bound; this replaces it with the measured figure.

cases.name: Bismarck (1940)
cases.source: kbismarck.com testing-period record: the plant designed for 138,000 hp and 29 knots 'actually obtained 150,170 hp and 30.1 knots'
cases.note: The 146-case reference set lists this ship at 138,000 hp / 30.0 kn, i.e. design power against a speed between design and trial; scoring against the trial figure moves the error from +14.2 % to +6.4 %.
